$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.macro. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-CURLY-CTORS-NONE
arms.note: no branch ctor reads as a CURLY block, so the shape-aware separator sends every value-`if` branch to the hardline arm and the `} else` join stops firing

arms.name: M-GAP-BLOCK-COMMENT-BREAKS
arms.note: a block comment in the gap before an inlineSep field is followed by a break again, so the first write leaves it on the metadata's line and a second write moves it

arms.name: M-ENDTYPE-BLOCK-COMMENT-ONLY
arms.note: a body of comments only takes end-edge blanks, the form decided to have none

arms.name: M-ENDABS-ORPHAN-LINE-BLANK
arms.note: enum abstract takes the class-kind forced blank before a line-comment orphan trail

arms.name: M-ENDTYPE-TRAIL-SRC-BLANK
arms.note: the source blank in front of orphan comments also opens a blank before the close curly under keep

arms.name: M-ENDTYPE-TYPEDEF-EMPTY
arms.note: a typedef body of comments only takes end-edge blanks, the form decided to have none

arms.name: M-ENDTYPE-TYPEDEF-TRAIL
arms.note: a typedef body ending in orphan comments takes no end-edge blanks after them

arms.name: M-ENDTYPE-BLOCK-TRAIL
arms.note: a body ending in orphan comments takes no end-edge blanks, the pre-fix placement

arms.name: M-SCAN-LOOP-FOLLOW-IGNORED
arms.note: a loop overlapping what follows it compiles to a scan that never gives an iteration back, so `[a-z]*[a-z0-9]` misses `ab`

arms.name: M-SCAN-ALT-OVERLAP-IGNORED
arms.note: an alternation whose branches begin alike compiles to a scan that commits to the first branch holding, so `a|ab` ends `ab` after `a`

arms.name: M-SBE-UNGATED
arms.find: final emit: Expr = dropTest == null ? policyDispatch : macro (_sbeSibling && $dropTest ? _de() : $policyDispatch);
arms.replace: final emit: Expr = dropTest == null ? policyDispatch : macro ($dropTest ? _de() : $policyDispatch);
arms.note: the optional `;` drop stops being gated on a following sibling, so an else-less value-`if` loses the terminator its enclosing statement needs

arms.name: M-TRAILOPT-KEEP-OFF
arms.note: no if / else / for / while body writes back its `@:trailOpt(';')` slot, so the `;` after a `}` is dropped by the formatter and the `;` after an unterminated `#if` region body is lost, failing the next statement with `Missing ;`

arms.name: M-TRAILOPT-KEEP-PRESENCE-BLIND
arms.note: the body slot stops reading source presence, so a region whose branches carry their own `;` gains a second one after `#end`

arms.name: M-SSB-TRAILSEMI-GATE-OFF
arms.note: a mandatory body's kept `;` no longer holds its braces under brace removal, so `for (…) { x; };` is de-braced into `for (…) x;;`, which Haxe rejects

arms.name: M-TRAILSEP-KEEP-OFF
arms.note: a block's trailing `;` after a `stmtNoSemi` element is dropped again, so `#end;` before `}` loses the only terminator of the region's last branch and `switch … {};` loses a source token

arms.name: M-CATCH-TRAILOPT-OFF
arms.find:
// A statement body's `;` (`catch (e) { … };`) is a source token like the mandatory path's.
pushStmtBodyTrailOpt(optParts, trailOptText, structTrailOptAccess);
arms.note: an optional statement body without a keyword (the last `catch` body) stops writing back its `@:trailOpt(';')` slot, so `try … catch (e) { … };` loses its `;` to the formatter

arms.name: M-GLUE-TO-PREVIOUS-OFF
arms.note: a stray member or case-body `;` is written on its own line again (`}` newline `;`) and the blank line before the next member is lost

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-COMPACT-OFF
arms.note: a wrapped function-type signature keeps the cascade's additional unit in every position, so its continuation sits two units past its line instead of one

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-NEST-RESET-OFF
arms.note: an anon field written inside a type argument still counts as nested, so its function type keeps the additional unit although the field starts a line of its own

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-NEST-RESET-PLAIN-OFF
arms.note: the plain writer keeps an anon field inside a type argument or parentheses nested, so its function type gets one unit more than the trivia writer gives the same field

arms.name: M-GLUE-ELEM-TEST-OFF
arms.note: no Star glues an element: the plain writer puts a member `;` on its own line and a space before a case body `;`

arms.name: M-SEP-GLUE-OFF
arms.note: an element's separator goes after its trailing comment again, so `#end; // c` comments out its own terminator and `fmt` refuses the file

arms.name: M-TRY-BODY-SYM-OFF
arms.note: the try BODY stops going through `SingleStmtBraces.trySymmetryBody`, so a bare body opposite a braced catch keeps its asymmetry instead of gaining a block of its own

arms.name: M-TRY-CATCHES-SYM-OFF
arms.note: the catch LIST stops going through `SingleStmtBraces.trySymmetryCatches`, so a braced group never de-braces and every catch but the last keeps the `;` Haxe rejects in front of `catch`

arms.name: M-NONCURLY-SAME-DROP
arms.note: a `[ … ]` block ctor separator falls back to the curly switch, where `SameOnBlock` matches no case and lands on the default space - so a bracket branch the `next` layout moved to its own line glues its `else` to the `]` (`[1] else if (b)` / `[] else`)

arms.name: M-VIF-SEAM-BRACKET-REFUSED
arms.note: the `expressionIfFit` soft pre-`else` seam is refused after a `[ … ]` branch as well as after a curly one, so a fitting bracket chain written as the ladder can never collapse onto one line

arms.name: M-VIF-SEAM-GLUE-BLIND
arms.find: final fitGate: Expr = glueTest == null ? macro _vifFit : macro (_vifFit && !$glueTest);
arms.note: the `expressionIfFit` soft pre-`else` seam ignores the bracket hug, so a `]` the knob glues to its `else` is split onto two lines whenever the fit group breaks

arms.name: M-NEWLINE-SIGNALS-NONE
arms.note: no downstream field contributes a captured-newline signal, so the conditional-expression seam has nothing to read and the source ladder collapses onto one line

arms.name: M-WORDOP-NO-RESTORE
arms.note: the operator loop stops rewinding to `_preWsPos` when the token that ended it is a WORD operator, so the trivia the loop consumed is lost and a conditional region after a metadata block no longer parses

arms.name: M-BLANK-MULTILINE-OFF
arms.find: if (gapRule == null) return { markExpr: macro {}, seenExpr: macro {}, applyExpr: macro {} };
arms.replace: if (true) return { markExpr: macro {}, seenExpr: macro {}, applyExpr: macro {} };
arms.note: the knob wires empty mark/seen/apply splices whatever the grammar asked for, so nothing measures a multiline member and no blank is inserted around one

arms.name: M-SSB-WRAP-DIRECTION
arms.find: final isThenBodyExpr: Expr = elseFieldName != null ? macro true : macro false;
arms.note: an `if` then-body stops identifying itself as one, so it is exempted from gate 8 alongside the loop bodies and a bare then opposite a braced else is never wrapped

arms.name: M-SSB-TRAIL-COMMENT-OFF
arms.note: the de-braced statement's same-line trailing comment is never hoisted, so it stays inside the block the unwrap just removed and leaves the output

arms.name: M-SSB-FRAME-OFF
arms.find:
final ssbSuppressCond: Null<Expr> = elseAccess == null
	? null
arms.note: the `_setSsbSuppress` frame is never armed, so an unwrap nested inside a then-body stops being gated on the trailing `else` and a dangling else loses the braces that keep it bound

arms.name: M-SSB-CHAIN-OFF
arms.find:
final thenChainSuppressExpr: Expr = elseAccess == null
	? macro false
arms.replace:
final thenChainSuppressExpr: Expr = true
	? macro false
arms.note: chain symmetry stops forcing braces, so one keeper branch of an else-if chain no longer makes its bare siblings keep theirs

arms.name: M-EICR-KNOB-IGNORED
arms.note: the runtime gate stops reading `opt.elseIfCommentReflow`, so the reflow fires with the knob off and every pre-knob layout moves

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-POLICY-BLIND
arms.find: final loopPolicy: Expr = loopIfElseTest == null ? optFlag : macro ($loopIfElseTest ? $nextPat : $optFlag);
arms.note: the loop-body `if`/`else` shape stops substituting `Next` for the placement, so `loopBodyIfElseNext` is inert at every `forBody` / `whileBody` / `doWhileBody` value and the reported site glues again

arms.name: M-COND-KIND-NAME-CONVENTION
arms.replace:
return collectKinds(declaring -> fieldRuleRefs(declaring).exists(ref -> reachesCondSeed(ref, seeds, [])))
			.filter(kind -> StringTools.startsWith(kind, 'CondSplice'));
arms.note: the derived vocabulary is filtered back to the grammar's NAMING convention, so the two ctors that already break it - `CondSharedBodyDecl`, named for a declaration region rather than a splice, and `MetaCondStmt`, named for the metadata it dispatches on - fall out of the gate, which is the hole a prefix list could never close

arms.name: M-PEB-WS-REWIND-OFF
arms.note: the block-ended byte check reads _prevEndPos - 1 raw, so an element that consumed trailing whitespace (a missed @:trailOpt, or the Pratt loop declining to rewind) hides its own `;` and the Star throws expected-separator

arms.name: M-BRACKET-GLUE-NONE
arms.note: no branch value ever reads as a bracket block the knob may hug, so a `[`-valued branch stops joining its head and the close stops cuddling the `else`

arms.name: M-ELSE-SWITCH-TESTS-NONE
arms.note: the `elseSwitch` knob contributes no case, so the policy selector never substitutes and `same` leaves the `switch` on its own line whatever the config asked for

arms.name: M-ELSE-SWITCH-CLOSE-NONE
arms.note: no branch body ever reads as a `switch` the knob glued to its head, so the pre-`else` gap falls back to the shape-aware hardline and a glued then-`switch` closes under an `else` on its own line

arms.name: M-ELSE-SWITCH-CLOSE-COMMENT
arms.note: the close-side glue stops asking whether a captured comment forced the body onto its own line, so the `else` cuddles a `}` that never moved up to the `if` head

arms.name: M-PEB-WS-REWIND-TRYPARSE-OFF
arms.note: the tryparse Star's own copy of the block-ended byte check reads _prevEndPos - 1 raw, so a `#if` region's statement whose terminator was swallowed hides its `;`, the loop breaks at the missing sep and the enclosing @:trail('#end') no longer matches - the file stops parsing

arms.name: M-PEB-WS-REWIND-SEPSTARTS-OFF
arms.note: the enum-branch lead/trail Star's own copy of the byte check reads _prevEndPos - 1 raw, so a nested `{ … }` block whose statement swallowed its own terminator refuses the following statement and the file stops parsing

arms.name: M-SEPSTAR-RESTPROBE-UNGATED
arms.note: the non-trivia struct-Star dispatch goes back to the macro-time constant, so a list below a case pattern charges the trailing guard to its own fit again

arms.name: M-TRIVIASEP-RESTPROBE-UNGATED
arms.note: the trivia dispatch stops reading the pattern flag, so a @:trivia Star below a case pattern rest-probes while the plain writer does not

arms.name: M-FILEHEADER-HEAD-NOT-PIU
arms.note: no module head ever classifies as package / import / using, so a real file header above one of them loses its blank line

arms.name: M-FILEHEADER-HEAD-ALWAYS-PIU
arms.note: every module head classifies as package / import / using, so a lone doc comment above a type is treated as a file header and a blank splits it from what it documents

arms.name: M-FILEHEADER-ANY-DECL
arms.note: the first-decl guard goes, so a doc comment leading the SECOND declaration is read as the module's file header

arms.name: M-FILEHEADER-ANY-COMMENT
arms.note: the first-comment guard goes, so the SECOND comment of a leading run is a file header too and a type's own doc is split from it

arms.name: M-FILEHEADER-ANY-COMMENT-KIND
arms.note: the block-comment guard goes, so a line-comment header takes the file-header blank the knob reserves for a block one

arms.name: M-FILEHEADER-NO-TWO-COMMENT-ARM
arms.note: the two-comments arm goes, so a header comment standing above a type's own doc with no package / import / using anywhere keeps no blank between them

arms.name: M-FILEHEADER-COND-OPAQUE
arms.note: the module-head #if stops being transparent, so a file header above a guarded import block reads as leading a type and loses its blank

arms.name: M-SSB-FRAME-BLANKET
arms.note: the suppress frame is armed without the span-precision probe, so a then-body that renders WITH its braces still gates every unwrap nested inside it

arms.name: M-ELSE-SEP-EXPR-BLIND
arms.note: the semicolon-next-line `else` rule stops asking whether it is at expression position, so a value-`if` inside a case body is governed by the statement rule

arms.name: M-ELSEIF-NEXT-OFF
arms.find: final elseIfCases: Array<Case> = [{ values: [kpNextPat], expr: nextLayoutExpr, guard: null }];
arms.note: the body wrap stops honouring `elseIf: next`, so a nested `if` under `else` stays glued to its keyword

arms.name: M-BEFORE-KW-TRAILING-DROP
arms.note: the gap before an optional keyword loses its BeforeKwTrailing layer, so a same-line trailing comment on the statement in front of `else` is dropped

arms.name: M-BEFORE-KW-LEADING-DROP
arms.note: the gap before an optional keyword loses its BeforeKwLeading layer, so an own-line comment written between a closing brace and `else` is dropped

arms.name: M-BEFORE-LEADING-COMMENT-DROP
arms.note: a bare non-first Ref emits the plain inter-field separator, so the comments captured in the BeforeLeading gap - a multiline block comment between a member modifier and the `var` keyword - never reach the output

arms.name: M-KWLEAD-NEVER-WORD
arms.note: no `@:lead` ever reads as starting with a word character, so the keyword's trailing space is stripped in front of a word lead too and `static var` / `static final` come out glued - after which the writer cannot re-parse its own output

arms.name: M-BLOCK-SHAPE-EQUIV-NONE
arms.note: no branch is block-shape equivalent - both disjuncts go, the block ctor and the `@:fmt(blockShape)` flag - so the bare try-catch ctor contributes no ctor pattern and the shape-aware separator glues `catch` onto the bare body instead of breaking the way the braced form does

arms.name: M-KWREF-BARE-BODY-BREAKS-BLIND
arms.note: a sub-struct whose first field carries `@:fmt(bareBodyBreaks)` stops stripping the keyword's trailing space, so a de-braced `try` is written with two spaces before its bare body and the second pass no longer reproduces the first

arms.name: M-KWREF-TIGHT-LEAD-BLIND
arms.note: a `default` branch's sub-struct opening on a tight `:` lead stops stripping the keyword's trailing space, so a `default` label is written `default :`

arms.name: M-PROJECTED-KINDS-ALT-ONLY
arms.note: the projected vocabulary loses its @:spanned half, so CatchClause / KeyValueBinder / VarMore stop being projected while the six kind sets that declare them keep naming them - the exact fail-open shape the differential exists to see, and the census floors stay satisfied so only the subset assertion goes red

arms.name: M-FOR-BODY-PROBE-EAGER
arms.find: final finalWrapExpr: Expr = wrapBodyAllman(opts, wrapExpr, writeCall, glueLayoutExpr, optFlag);
arms.replace: final finalWrapExpr: Expr = wrapBodyAllman(opts, macro { final _eagerProbe: anyparse.core.Doc = $bodyDoc; $wrapExpr; }, writeCall, glueLayoutExpr, optFlag);
arms.note: an Allman-bearing body is written again by an eager probe beside the bound `_bpBody`, so a comprehension nest writes its innermost body 2^depth times

arms.name: M-CHAIN-WALK-EAGER
arms.note: the method-chain walk writes every call's arguments before it knows the value is a chain, and the plain call writes them again, so `a.m(a.m(…))` doubles per level

arms.name: M-SPANINFO-BOUND-MORE
arms.note: only a type parameter's first bound is kept, the `& Type` tail is dropped

arms.name: M-KWTRAIL-FLAT-GAP-KEPT
arms.note: a flat gap after a trailing line comment stays flat, so `else` lands on the comment's line and the round trip refuses the file

arms.name: M-KWTRAIL-GUARD-HARD
arms.note: a gap that already opens with a break gets a second one, so a trailing comment followed by an own-line comment gains a blank line

arms.name: M-CLOSE-TRAIL-BLOCK-BREAKS
arms.note: a close-trailing comment is followed by a forward hardline whatever its style again, so `} /* c */` breaks before a same-line `else` / `while` / `catch`

arms.name: M-CLOSE-TRAIL-EMPTY-HARD
arms.find: final emptyTrailExpr: Expr = macro _dc([_dt($v{emptyText}), trailingCommentDocGuarded(_trailClose, opt)]);
arms.replace: final emptyTrailExpr: Expr = macro _dc([_dt($v{emptyText}), trailingCommentDocVerbatim(_trailClose, opt), _dhl()]);
arms.note: an empty block's close-trailing comment is followed by a hard newline again, so a block comment breaks and a line comment pushes the keyword one space out

arms.name: M-CATCH-CLOSE-TRAIL-ANY
arms.note: the first-catch separator is dropped after ANY close-trailing comment again, so `} /* c */catch` loses its gap under every policy

arms.name: M-OPEN-TRAIL-EMPTY-UNGUARDED
arms.note: `{ /* n */ } // c` emits its line comment with no forward break, so the keyword after it is swallowed into the comment

arms.name: M-OPEN-TRAIL-SEP-UNGUARDED
arms.note: `(/* n */) // c` emits its line comment with no forward break, so the function body's `{` is swallowed into the comment

arms.name: M-FNBODY-GAP-COMMENT-NONE
arms.note: the function body's `BeforeLeading` slot goes unread again, so `function f():Int /* c */ {` drops the comment

arms.name: M-BEFORE-LEAD-CAPTURE-NONE
arms.note: an optional lead commit forgets the block comment before its lead, so `var x /* c */ = 1` drops it

arms.name: M-BEFORE-LEAD-MANDATORY-NONE
arms.note: a mandatory lead skips the block comment before it as whitespace again, so `{x /* c */:Int}` drops it

arms.name: M-BEFORE-LEAD-WRITER-OPT-NONE
arms.note: an optional lead's captured comment is never written, so `var x /* c */ = 1` drops it

arms.name: M-BEFORE-LEAD-WRITER-MANDATORY-NONE
arms.note: a mandatory lead's captured comment is never written, so `{x /* c */:Int}` drops it

arms.name: M-JSON-KEY-PARSE
arms.note: a ByName parser matches a field by its Haxe name, so a key declared with `@:key` (a keyword, a hyphenated key) is never read

arms.name: M-JSON-KEY-WRITE
arms.note: a ByName writer spells a field by its Haxe name, so what it writes its own parser cannot read back

arms.name: M-JSON-KEY-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a `@:key` that is not one string literal is ignored, and the field silently keeps its Haxe name as its key

arms.name: M-JSON-KEY-UNWRITABLE
arms.note: a key holding a quote or a backslash builds, and the writer emits a document no JSON parser reads

arms.name: M-JSON-KEY-DUPLICATES
arms.note: two fields spelled with one key build, and the parser fills only the first

arms.name: M-JSON-KEY-DUP-AT-FIELD
arms.note: two fields sharing a key are reported at the build macro, not at the field

arms.name: M-DOWHILE-PLAIN-SEMI
arms.note: the plain writer emits `do i++; while (c)` again, which Haxe rejects (`Expected while`)

arms.name: M-WALK-TYPE-ARGS-UNCOUNTED
arms.note: the walker records no type-argument count, so the matcher sees one flat child run

arms.name: M-XREN-EXTENDS-HEAD-UNEMITTED
arms.find: final head: Null<Expr> = nominal ? nameOfValue(child, access) : null;
arms.note: a nominal reference reached through a `type` slot emits no head again, so a struct extension nested in an annotation (`Array<{ > T, }>`) projects its fields' types and never `T`

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-OFF
arms.note: no trial is moved: every enum-branch trial stays inline in its rule and BranchOutliningTest reads the unchanged body

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-WRITE-BLIND
arms.find: refuse('a write to the rule local $name');
arms.note: a trial that writes a rule local is moved, so the helper writes its own copy and the rule never sees the write

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-BREAK-BLIND
arms.find: if (_loops == 0) refuse('a break / continue that leaves the trial');
arms.note: a break that leaves the trial is moved into a helper, where it has no loop to target

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-SWITCH-BLIND
arms.note: a trial holding a switch is moved although its pattern bindings are not scoped

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-FOR-PATTERN-BLIND
arms.find: refuse('a for over a non-identifier pattern');
arms.note: a for over a key-value pattern is moved although its bindings are not scoped

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-NULLABLE-RETURN-BLIND
arms.find: if (_fns == 0 && !cannotBeNull(value)) refuse('a return whose value may be null');
arms.note: a return that may hand back null is moved, and the call site reads that null as a failed trial and tries the next branch

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-CONSTANT-AS-CTOR
arms.note: an all-capitals constant counts as a constructor, so its possibly-null value is returned through a helper

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-UNTYPED-CAPTURE
arms.note: a captured rule local with no single declared type becomes a helper parameter without a type

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-NESTED-ALT-BLIND
arms.note: the outer trial of a moved nested trial returns _alt and stays inline

arms.name: M-QUERY-NAME-IGNORED
arms.note: a `@:queryName` field names nothing, so a JSON object member projects unnamed and `Member:<key>` matches no node

arms.name: M-PAREN-BROKEN-CHAIN-PINNED
arms.note: an expression paren around a `+`/`-` chain an operand already broke pins that chain flat again when no `expressionWrapping` rule is set, so every continuation line renders at column 0 and the next write re-indents it

arms.name: M-BREAKMARK-FIT-NAMED
arms.note: an `#if` body under `conditionalExprFit` is named too, though the region is already a named break of its own (`BreakCommits.namedRegion`), so a literal that fits its line and an object-literal rule keeps flat is broken

arms.name: M-DROPPED-SEP-UNREHOMED
arms.note: a list whose trailing separator the writer drops is laid out from the source tree, the comment outside the element the next parse reads it inside of

arms.name: M-TAIL-SLOT-OVERWRITTEN
arms.note: a struct close slot already holding a comment is overwritten, and that comment is lost

arms.name: M-TAIL-ALT-SLOT-OVERWRITTEN
arms.note: a ctor close slot already holding a comment is overwritten, and that comment is lost

arms.name: M-TAIL-WRITTEN-SEMICOLON-IGNORED
arms.note: a body the source closed with `;` takes the comment in front of the `;`, which the comment then swallows

arms.name: M-TAIL-ONLY-KNOWN-METAS
arms.note: a shape with a token after its operand (a paren pair, a trail literal) passes the comment into the operand, ahead of that token

arms.name: M-TAIL-ABSENT-FIELD-STOPS
arms.note: an absent optional last field (an if with no else) answers null instead of the field emitted before it

arms.name: M-TAIL-ARRAY-SLOT-UNREAD
arms.note: an array literal tail no longer takes the comment its close captures

arms.name: M-TAIL-CALL-SLOT-UNREAD
arms.note: a call tail no longer takes the comment its close paren captures

arms.name: M-TAIL-INFIX-UNREAD
arms.find: if (branch.hasMeta(':infix')) return children.length == 2 && onlyMetas(branch, [':infix', ':fmt']) ? Operand(1) : None;
arms.note: an infix expression's right operand is not asked, so `t + {a: 1}` keeps the comment outside

arms.name: M-TAIL-TERNARY-UNREAD
arms.find: if (branch.hasMeta(':ternary')) return children.length == 3 && onlyMetas(branch, [':ternary', ':fmt']) ? Operand(2) : None;
arms.note: a ternary's else operand is not asked

arms.name: M-TAIL-PREFIX-UNREAD
arms.find: if (branch.hasMeta(':prefix')) return children.length == 1 && onlyMetas(branch, [':prefix', ':fmt']) ? Operand(0) : None;
arms.note: a prefix operator's operand is not asked

arms.name: M-TAIL-OPERAND-UNREAD
arms.find: return single && onlyMetas(branch, TRANSPARENT_BRANCH_METAS) ? Operand(0) : None;
arms.note: a keyword or lead ctor (if, for, object literal, new, function) does not pass the comment to its one operand

arms.name: M-REGION-UNNAMED
arms.note: a fit region is an undecided group again, so a call filling its line measures it flat and opens before the `#if` the next write glues

arms.name: M-REGION-SEAMS-BOUNDED
arms.note: the elseifs Star of a fit region keeps its force-flat boundary, so inside a glued comprehension body the seams before the #elseif flatten and the ones after it break

arms.name: M-STMT-LIST-CALLARG-BARRIER
arms.note: a statement-list element keeps the call-argument chain flag: the first chain in a lambda argument's body wraps its operator at the statement's indent

arms.name: M-STMT-LIST-CALLARG-BLOCK
arms.note: a block statement (lambda / anonymous function body) bypasses the statement-list barrier and inherits the call-argument chain flag

arms.name: M-STMT-LIST-CALLARG-CASE
arms.note: a case-body statement of an arrow-body switch argument bypasses the statement-list barrier and inherits the call-argument chain flag

arms.name: M-TCO-KNOB-IGNORED
arms.note: the runtime gate stops reading `opt.trailingCommentAbove`, so every opted-in block moves its overflowing trailing comments with the knob off

arms.name: M-TCO-LEADING-IGNORED
arms.note: an element that already carries a leading comment moves its trailing one too, where the second pass reads a longer leading list and the blank / doc / run rules may answer differently

arms.name: M-CHAIN-REST-UNSET
arms.note: no `&&` / `+` chain is rest-aware, so every one-or-two-column overrun breaks inside an operand or not at all

arms.name: M-CHAIN-REST-IN-KEPT-PAREN
arms.note: a chain inside a paren that owns the wrap counts the paren's rest too, so it breaks where the paren should open first

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-COUNTED
arms.note: a source-flat list its cascade commits to one-per-line reaches its host counted while the next write reads it back deferred, so a chain or an arrow around it breaks once and glues on the next write

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-ANY-RESULT
arms.note: every source-flat list is deferred, a flat one included, so a host under-measures a literal that still stands flat and glues past the limit

arms.name: M-SPANINFO-RETURN-SOURCES
arms.note: the span info records no return type source, so no signature reads one

arms.name: M-CATCH-BLOCK-LINE-END-GLUED
arms.note: a block comment that ended its source line after the try body's `}` glues the first `catch` onto its line again under a same-line policy

arms.name: M-TRAIL-FORCEMULTI-UNGATED
arms.note: a list laid out one item per line by a comment appends the trailing comma after a region ending it

arms.name: M-TRAIL-CALL-FORCEMULTI-UNGATED
arms.note: call arguments laid out one per line by a line comment append the trailing comma after a region ending them

arms.name: M-CASCADE-LEAD-BREAKS
arms.note: the wrap cascade breaks after a block comment the source glued to its parameter, so the next write moves the parameter
